question: A certain sum of money doubles itself in 16 years on simple interest. In how many years it will be six times?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In Simple Interest, amount grows linearly with time

Doubling means interest = 1P in 16 years

Six times means interest = 5P

Time ∝ Interest ⇒ Required time = 16 × 5

**∴ Answer = 80 years**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

A sum doubles in 16 years on simple interest

**Formula used:**

Simple Interest = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

**Calculation:**

⇒ When amount doubles ⇒ SI = P

⇒ So, P = (P × R × 16) ÷ 100

⇒ 1 = (R × 16) ÷ 100

⇒ R = 100 ÷ 16

⇒ Now for six times ⇒ SI = 5P

⇒ 5P = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

⇒ 5 = (R × T) ÷ 100

⇒ 5 = ((100 ÷ 16) × T) ÷ 100

⇒ 5 = T ÷ 16

⇒ T = 80 years

**∴ The correct answer is 80 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest Growth

In SI, interest increases linearly with time. Amount = P + SI.

Doubling Time

If principal doubles in T years, then SI earned = P in T years.

Multiplication Rule

If amount becomes n times, SI = (n − 1)P, and time scales accordingly.
